questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the main language was english and that it was a city i wanted to live in and explore.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the contact person was very good at providing thorough information and guides.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Once I arrived we still recieved some emails from the contact person, and on the first day there were orientation were a lot of information was given as well as ressources to use for help during our stay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Through the university they had an agreement with 3 different accommodations all in a dorm style, where only one was on campus and the other two were located very close to campus.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
At the Queen Mary Building (the one on campus) there was a communal kitchen that was shared by all residents
For the other two options I believe there were meal plans, were all or some meals were provided.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
It is a big campus, so it will take some time to walk from the accommodation to the main part of campus (around 15 min.)
It is quite expensive for what you get, but everything else is equally if not more expensive and in my opinion it is a good option for peace of mind as you get it sorted well before departure.
It is very nice to live in the same building as other exchange students (most students living there are international students) and cook together as well as use the different amenities such as movie room, rooftop and attend the different activities hosted by the staff of the accommodation.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You get a login to a website where you list the units you wish to undertake (list 10, but you will only enrol in 4) and these are then approved or denied by the department depending on if you have the prerequisites. Then you choose the 4 you wish to take and a few weeks before school starts you can state preferences for your timetable.
It is possible to change the chosen units before school starts and during the first few weeks.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The contact person sent emails with guides on how to do everything and was available for questions, so it was not difficult to do.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was approved for 8/10 of the ones I listed so I could easily choose 4 and also managed to change a unit during the orientation week with no issue.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Take your time and follow the guide.
Spend time early to make a list of the subjects that you might be interested in so this can be narrowed down as opposed to only having 4 and then scrambling to finde others if it doesn't work out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two 2000 level courses (2nd year), and two 3000 level courses (3rd year).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The exam is only worth around 50% of the grade and the rest comes from assignments, reports and quizzes during the semester so you have work to do, and this is often group work. Some units have no exam and so the grade is based entirely on what you do during the semester.
I had no books and very little assigned reading compared to KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Australian Wildlife Biology
Biology Experimental Design and Analysis
Beyond the Genome
International Health

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed Australian Wildlife Biology as it was very informative and we got to go to the zoo 5 times as part of the teachings. Many other exchange students took it and so it was not expected that you had any previous knowledge on animals or biology.

questions.answer: There were some fees for the accommodation as well as a deposit of around a months rent which I had not budgeted with

questions.answer: The visa was more expensive that i thought it was around 3500 DKK but transportation was very cheap and a trip with bus usually only costed around 5 DKK

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were SO many different clubs - pretty much everything you could think of.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The yoga club was very good and cheaper than studios.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Definitely do a surf camp!
Blue mountains is also very nice to visit and spend a weekend in.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: quite easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing was challenging, maybe the Australian accent and slang could be a bit difficult sometimes.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness and helpfulness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy it, try and find a balance between taking some rewarding units but also some that are a bit easier so you can have more free time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met during my stay and the friendships we build as well as the experiences we shared.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: With the time difference you could sometimes feel a bit lonely and cut off from everyone back home, as they usually woke up when you day was almost finished.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
